continuous random variable: takes values on an interval of the real number line, so the number of possible values is uncountably infinite; e.g. the weight of a random person in kg. See [Continuous random variables: why P(X = x) = 0](#/math3042-u5/continuous-random-variables).
continuous probability distribution: the distribution of a continuous variable, described by a density $f(x)$ and areas rather than by $P(x)$ for single values; $P(X = x) = 0$ for every individual $x$. See [Continuous random variables: why P(X = x) = 0](#/math3042-u5/continuous-random-variables).
uniform distribution: the simplest continuous distribution, flat on an interval $[a, b]$ with height $1/(b-a)$; $P(c \le X \le d) = (d-c)/(b-a)$; the bus-wait example on $[0, 20]$ minutes. See [The uniform distribution: waiting for the bus](#/math3042-u5/uniform).
probability density function|pdf|f(x): a function $f(x) \ge 0$ with total area 1 such that $P(X \le b) = \int_{-\infty}^{b} f(x)\,dx$; probabilities are areas under it. See [Probability density functions and F(x)](#/math3042-u5/pdf-cdf).
cumulative probability function|cdf|F(x): $F(x) = P(X \le x) = \int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t)\,dt$; then $P(a \le X \le b) = F(b) - F(a)$. See [Probability density functions and F(x)](#/math3042-u5/pdf-cdf).
normal distribution|Gaussian: the bell-shaped distribution, symmetric about $\mu$, with inflection points at $\mu \pm \sigma$ and pdf $f(x) = e^{-\frac12((x-\mu)/\sigma)^2}/(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$; written $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$. See [The normal distribution: shape, mu and sigma](#/math3042-u5/normal-distribution).
inflection point: where the bell curve changes from bending down to bending up, at a distance $\sigma$ from the centre. See [The normal distribution: shape, mu and sigma](#/math3042-u5/normal-distribution).
standard normal distribution|Z-distribut: the normal distribution with $\mu = 0$ and $\sigma = 1$, whose areas are tabulated; $f(z) = e^{-z^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$. See [The standard normal distribution and the Z table](#/math3042-u5/standard-normal-z-table).
Z table|table of standard normal probabi: the table of $P(Z \le z)$ for $z$ to two decimals; right tails by $1 -$, intervals by subtraction; read backwards for percentiles (0.95 ↔ 1.645). See [The standard normal distribution and the Z table](#/math3042-u5/standard-normal-z-table).
standardize|Z = (X − μ)/σ: the key idea: if $X$ is normal with mean $\mu$ and sd $\sigma$, then $Z = (X - \mu)/\sigma$ follows the standard normal, so one table serves every normal variable. See [Standardizing: IQ, cosmic radiation, Gaussian noise](#/math3042-u5/normal-applications).
percentile of a normal variable: the $x$ with $P(X \le x) = p$: look up $z$ for $p$ in the table, then $x = \mu + z\sigma$ (95th: $z = 1.645$). See [Standardizing: IQ, cosmic radiation, Gaussian noise](#/math3042-u5/normal-applications).
Gaussian noise: channel noise modelled as a normal random variable (the bit-error example: $\mu = 0$ V, $\sigma = 0.22$ V, a 0-bit at 2 V read as 1 when noise exceeds 0.5 V). See [Standardizing: IQ, cosmic radiation, Gaussian noise](#/math3042-u5/normal-applications).
exponential distribution: the model for waiting time in a memory-less system, $f(x) = \frac1\beta e^{-x/\beta}$ for $x \ge 0$, $F(x) = 1 - e^{-x/\beta}$, $\mu = \beta$, $\sigma = \beta$. See [The exponential distribution: waiting between requests](#/math3042-u5/exponential).
beta|β: the exponential distribution's parameter, equal to the mean waiting time (2.5 s between requests; 2 minutes per customer when the rate is 30 per hour); R's `rate` is $1/\beta$. See [The exponential distribution: waiting between requests](#/math3042-u5/exponential).
memoryless: given that some time has already passed, the remaining wait has the same exponential distribution as a fresh one: $P(2.5 \le X \le 3.5 \mid X > 1) = P(1.5 \le X \le 2.5)$. See [Percentiles and the memoryless property: the bank teller](#/math3042-u5/exponential-memoryless).
pnorm|qnorm|pexp|qexp|punif: R's cumulative probability (p) and quantile (q) functions for the normal, exponential and uniform distributions; `pnorm(120, 100, 15)` = 0.9088, `qnorm(0.95)` = 1.645, `pexp(4, rate=1/2.5)` = 0.7981. See [punif, pnorm, qnorm, pexp, qexp and curve()](#/math3042-u5/continuous-in-r).
